introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), June 2019, ADVANCED LEVEL. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure considered as an attempt to cheat will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorized composition will earn you no marks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**QUESTION 2: TEXT RECONSTRUCTION (15 marks)**

Read the following passage carefully. Then without altering the numbering, copy and complete the reconstructed form that follows it by filling in the blanks with the correct expressions.

To obtain sugar from cane, the producer must carefully follow these steps:

The farmer must harvest the cane as soon as it reaches the last growth period. Many farmers still cut a lot of cane by hand using machetes, although this is expensive. Large scale farmers use mechanical harvesters to cut cane on large plantations. Either way, the harvesters cut the cane close to the ground and strip the leaves from the stalks. They then chop the stripped cane into convenient lengths that you can mill.

At this stage, you shred the cane into small pieces into the mill. This mill crushes the shredded cane and squeezes juice out of them. The producer has to spray a lot of water into the crushed cane to dilute the sugary liquid. You then heat the juice extract and add lime to clarify the juice and clear impurities from it. Transfer the clear juice into evaporators which heat it using steam coils. By the time it passes the last evaporator, the juice becomes a relatively thick syrup containing 40-50% of sugar. Distil the syrup at low pressure to produce massecuite which is a suspension of sugar crystals. This massecuite is usually in thick brown liquid. We then centrifuge the sugar crystals and force them onto a wire mesh on the sides of the centrifuge. In the final stage, wash the centrifugal sugar with steam, which leaves the product white. We remove the few traces of colour by dissolving the sugar into a syrup.

*Source: Secondary English Project For Cameroon.*

**RECONSTRUCTED FORM**

Mechanical harvesters ________ (2) to cut cane on large plantations. Either way, ________ (3) and ________ (4) from the stalks. The stripped cane are then ________ (5) into convenient lengths that ________ (6).

A this stage, the cane is shredded in pieces into the will. The cane ________ (7) in the mill and ________ (8) out of them. To dilute the sugary water, ________ (9). The juice extract ________ (10) and lime added to clear impurities from it. The clear juice ________ (11). By the time the juice ________ , (12) it becomes a relatively thick syrup containing 40-50% of sugar. The ________ (13) at low pressure to produce massecuite. The sugar crystals are centrifuged and forced onto a wire mesh on the side of the centrifuge. In the final stage, the centrifugal sugar ________ (14) with steam. The product is then left white. By dissolving the sugar into a syrup, ________ (15).
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reconstructed text (the answers are in bold; the printed faults of the form are kept)**

The cane **must be harvested** (1) as soon as it reaches the last growth period. Although this is expensive, machetes are employed to cut a lot of cane. Mechanical harvesters **are used** (2) to cut cane on large plantations. Either way, **the cane is cut close to the ground** (3) and **the leaves are stripped** (4) from the stalks. The stripped cane are then **chopped** (5) into convenient lengths that **can be milled** (6).

A this stage, the cane is shredded in pieces into the will. The cane **is crushed** (7) in the mill and **juice is squeezed** (8) out of them. To dilute the sugary water, **a lot of water has to be sprayed into the crushed cane** (9). The juice extract **is heated** (10) and lime added to clear impurities from it. The clear juice **is transferred into evaporators which heat it using steam coils** (11). By the time the juice **passes the last evaporator** (12), it becomes a relatively thick syrup containing 40-50% of sugar. The **syrup is distilled** (13) at low pressure to produce massecuite. The sugar crystals are centrifuged and forced onto a wire mesh on the side of the centrifuge. In the final stage, the centrifugal sugar **is washed** (14) with steam. The product is then left white. By dissolving the sugar into a syrup, **the few traces of colour are removed** (15).

**Before and after**

| No. | Active clause in the passage | Answer | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | must harvest the cane | must be harvested | modal verb + passive: must + be + past participle |
| 2 | use mechanical harvesters | are used | present passive, plural subject (harvesters) |
| 3 | the harvesters cut the cane close to the ground | the cane is cut close to the ground | object becomes subject; the agent is dropped |
| 4 | [the harvesters] strip the leaves from the stalks | the leaves are stripped | present passive, plural subject; "from the stalks" is already in the form |
| 5 | chop the stripped cane | chopped | "are then" is given, so only the past participle is needed |
| 6 | lengths that you can mill | can be milled | modal passive: can + be + past participle |
| 7 | this mill crushes the shredded cane | is crushed | present passive, singular subject (the cane) |
| 8 | [the mill] squeezes juice out of them | juice is squeezed | the object (juice) becomes the subject; "out of them" is already in the form |
| 9 | the producer has to spray a lot of water into the crushed cane | a lot of water has to be sprayed into the crushed cane | has to + be + past participle |
| 10 | you then heat the juice extract | is heated | "and lime added" follows: parallel passive without a second "is" |
| 11 | transfer the clear juice into evaporators which heat it using steam coils | is transferred into evaporators which heat it using steam coils | imperative becomes a present passive; "is transferred into evaporators where it is heated" is also accepted |
| 12 | by the time it passes the last evaporator | passes the last evaporator | a time clause keeps the active verb because the juice is the subject; "has passed" is also accepted |
| 13 | distil the syrup at low pressure | syrup is distilled | after "The", the noun and the passive verb are needed |
| 14 | wash the centrifugal sugar with steam | is washed | present passive |
| 15 | we remove the few traces of colour | the few traces of colour are removed | the gerund phrase "By dissolving..." needs a subject: the traces of colour are removed (a plural passive) |

**Method.** The task is to turn the instructions of the passage (active verbs, imperatives, "you" and "we") into an impersonal process written in the passive voice: the object of the active verb becomes the subject, the verb becomes be + past participle, and the doer (the farmer, the producer, the harvesters) is dropped because the process matters more than the people. Check agreement (singular or plural), the tense (present) and the words already printed after each blank.

**Marking.** One mark per correct blank is assumed (15 blanks, 15 marks); a form that keeps the meaning and is grammatically correct is accepted even if its wording differs slightly from the model.

**Common mistakes**

1. Keeping the active voice ("the harvesters cut") or the imperative ("transfer"), which does not fit the printed words around the blank.
2. Wrong agreement or form of the participle ("the leaves is stripped", "is chop"), or repeating words that are already printed after the blank.

incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». Section A obligatoire (aucune règle), Section B : 1 sujet sur 6 (a à f), Section C : 1 question sur 4. Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Fautes imprimées dans le sujet, laissées telles quelles : titre « SECTION A SUMMERY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION » (summary), « for few hours » (Q1), « A this stage », « into the will » (mill), « The stripped cane are then », « out of them » (Q2, forme reconstruite) ; Section C question 2 : « Use any Three prescribed text ».
Le tiret cadratin du passage de résumé (« choice of home - among the stinging tentacles ») est écrit « - » conformément à la règle du projet. Le passage ne porte pas de numéros de ligne imprimés.

Section A : le sujet imprime 30 marks pour la section (15 par question). La répartition des 15 points du résumé n'est pas imprimée : la grille du corrigé est indicative. La reconstruction est comptée à 1 point par blanc (15 blancs), ce qui est une hypothèse ; plusieurs réponses sont acceptables pour certains blancs (voir le corrigé).

Section B : 20 marks (Content and Organisation 6, Expression 8, Accuracy 6), 500 à 550 mots demandés. Points imprimés non corrigés. Compositions modèles : comptes de mots faits par script (de 517 à 534 mots).
